newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Labour Union pledges to defend the poor.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Labour Union pledges to defend the poor.

text.p: Poland's leftist opposition Labour Union (UP) party said on Sunday its parliamentary campaign will focus on defending those who did not benefit from the country's economic growth of the past years.
The leftist party also officially unveiled its election slogan of "You deserve more" for parliamentary polls due around September.
"Economic growth cannot serve only some of our citizens, everyone must have a chance," UP leader Ryszard Bugaj told public television news.
Bugaj said Poles were divided into two groups -- a minority who were reaping the fruits of the country's economic success and a majority who were losing the race.
UP said the four biggest challenges facing Poland were limiting unemployment, reforming medical care and education as well as solving the country's housing problems.

The Labour Union, rooted in the anti-communist opposition movement before 1989, has kept its distance from the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) despite similar views on many social and economic issues.
In recent opinion polls UP has recieved between five and 10 percent support.
